business_problem: TELUS Health One had outgrown a self-managed MongoDB Community Edition deployment and needed a more scalable, secure, and operationally mature cloud database for a global mental-health platform serving 50,000 employers and 10 million employees.
solution_summary: TELUS Health migrated TELUS Health One from self-managed MongoDB Community Edition to MongoDB Atlas to support a global mental-health platform serving web, iOS, and Android applications. Working with MongoDB Professional Services, the team assessed the legacy environment, ensured dependent services could run against both the old database and Atlas, then moved the full database in less than six months without breaking business continuity. Atlas now sits in the core layer of TELUS Health One's onion-style architecture behind the client apps, microservices layer, and monolithic services, while built-in encryption at rest and in transit reduces compliance risk for sensitive mental-health data. The team also adopted Atlas Charts for visibility into performance and plans to extend reporting with Data Federation as demand grows.

data_flow: TELUS Health One's web, iOS, and Android apps communicate with a microservices layer that passes requests to core monolithic services backed by MongoDB Atlas. Atlas stores the operational data, while Atlas Charts surfaces performance insights and the platform's encrypted data path helps protect sensitive health information.
business_outcome: TELUS Health migrated the full database in less than six months, largely eliminated self-managed scaling pain, accelerated some queries by nearly 30x, and strengthened privacy controls for a mission-critical healthcare application.
